📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a fresh feature PortuGOAL will be bringing you some recommended reading about Portuguese football from around the web, penned by our own network of writers or others.

Recent findings suggest that we kick off by alerting you to a superb interview in the Guardian by Nick Ames with Port Vale's Portuguese manager Bruno Ribeiro. The headline writer focused on Ribeiro's relationship with José Mourinho, but it is the detail of Ribeiro's struggle to make things work at an English third-tier team of meagre resources that makes for fascinating insight.

Benfica are top of the Liga NOS and their coach Rui Vitória continues to confound the doubters who believed he would not be up to the job at the Lisbon giants. Simon Curtis takes a look at "the quiet man at the helm of a national institution". And Benfica fans, while we've got your attention, a shout out for Tom Kundert's profile of the club's world-renowned Seixal Academy for ESPN.

Talking about Portuguese football schools, none has produced more top-class players in recent decades than Sporting's Alcochete Academy, and the excellent Outside of the Boot website has a brilliantly detailed profile written by Mateus Carvalho of another possible gem for the Lions, Francisco Geraldes, who is at the moment on loan at Moreirense.

To finish up this initial trip around the net, we alert you to FourFourTwo's list of the 59 best Under-21 footballers from around the world. The section we highlight has a mini profile of Porto striker André Silva, who will be hoping to net his first senior international goal tonight for the Seleção against Andorra. In case you're wondering, the British magazine rank him at number 23.

💡 Key Takeaways

Né à Firminy, conseiller municipal de Saint-Etienne (depuis 8 mois) et parlementaire le plus investi dans le soutien aux ultras stéphanois (il avait été un des premiers signataires de notre pétition lancée le printemps 2025 et ayant recueilli plus de 5 800 signatures), le député PS ligérien Pierrick Courbon (41 ans) a posté cet après-midi le message suivant sur son compte Instagram.

It has been revealed that "Ce qui s'est passé à Reims est inacceptable ! Les supporters ne sont pas des sous-citoyens, encore moins du bétail. Je saisis le Ministre de l'Intérieur. Malgré trois décisions de justice confirmant l'absence d'interdiction d'accès au stade tout comme les déplacements en autocars, les supporters stéphanois ont été interpellés à proximité du stade Auguste-Delaune, et contraints de faire demi-tour sous escorte policière. Il est indéniable que des erreurs ont été commises par les services de l'Etat, et qu'un contournement des décisions de justice a eu lieu.

Les supporters ne sont pas des sous-citoyens. Pourtant, depuis de nombreuses années, le supportérisme est un laboratoire commode de mesures sécuritaires et liberticides, qui ne seraient toélérées dans un autre pan de la société. Comme je m'y suis engagé dès samedi, je viens d'alerter Laurent Nunez pour demander des réponses et des explications. La gestion des supporters en France est catastrophique. Je continuerai de les défendre car l'enjeu dépasse le simple cadre sportif.".

It has been revealed that forest fires occur every summer in Portugal but the tragedy that struck the community of Pedrógão Grande in the centre of the country is unprecedented. Over 60 people lost their lives, many trapped in their cars when trying to flee from the flames.

Industry observers note that this Just Giving page is a simple way for people, wherever they are in the world, to make a contribution to help rebuild these communities and bring some comfort to those who lost everything in the blink of an eye. The money raised will be sent to a network of local authorities and charities working in the area affected. Thank you for your support.

💡 Key Takeaways

Recent findings suggest that les U15 de Benjamin Petit, après leur précieuse victoire d'il y a deux semaines contre Villefranche (1-0) se déplaçaient cet après-midi sur le terrain de l'AS Saint-Priest, qui n'est jamais un adversaire facile. Auparavant, dans la semaine, mercredi, à Cruas, ils s'étaient mesurés à l'Olympique de Marseille, leader de la poule Méditerranée, et qui, en match amical, a largement battu bon nombre d'équipes de renom. Les jeunes Verts avaient mieux fait que se défendre, ne s'inclinant que sur le score de 2 à 1. Revenons-en au match d'aujourd'hui pour dire que la victoire est revenue en toute logique aux jeunes Verts sur le score de 2 à 1, une victoire qui va leur permettre d'engranger des points et....de la confiance.

Ce sont les Sanpriods qui ont ouvert la marque, contre le cours du jeu, à la 19ème minute sur une approximation défensive. Mais les Verts réagissaient immédiatement et, deux minutes plus tard, à la 21ème, Kaïs Boukerma, sur une passe de Charly Davignon, de l'entrée de la surface, plaçait une frappe au ras du poteau pour l'égalisation. Un quart d'heure plus tard, à la 36ème, Hugo Bastide, qui opérait aujourd'hui en défense centrale, récupérait fort à propos un 2ème ballon sur un corner pour donner l'avantage aux Verts. Ce fut difficile après le repos, car Saint-Priest mettait la pression pour revenir au score. Mais les Verts faisaient preuve de solidarité et de rigueur défensive pour conserver cet avantage de 2 à 1.A noter la victoire des U14 sur le score de 8 à 1. Nous reviendrons ultérieurement sur la belle saison de cette équipe.

La composition : Clapeyron - Bergougnoux, Wojcik, Bastide, Uneau - Boukerma, Lebreton (L.La Rosa, 45ème), M.La Rosa (Linganzi Koumba, 40ème) - Fernandes (Moutae, 50ème), Bangoura, Davignon.

La réaction de Benjamin Petit : "Nous avons fait une bonne première mi-temps, même si nous avons un peu manqué de tranchant dans le domaine offensif. Il n'a pas manqué grand chose sur plusieurs situations intéressantes. C'est là un axe de progrès bien identifié que d'aller chercher cette réussite offensive. J'ai apprécié le fait que les garçons soient restés sereins après l'ouverture du score par Saint-Priest. Cela leur a permis de revenir rapidement et de passer devant avant la pause. Par contre, la deuxième mi-temps a été plus compliquée. Saint-Priest nous a mis la pression et nous avons eu plus de mal à construire et à progresser à l'intérieur du jeu. Mais nous avons fait preuve de caractère, de rigueur défensive et cela nous a permis de conserver le résultat.".

Glasner made to wait for first win as Trafford thwarts Forest

📅 25 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4152 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.
  • Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.
  • The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

James Trafford became the record signing for a British goalkeeper this summer and he is already proving invaluable for Leeds United.

Signed from Manchester City for an initial £40m in August, Trafford has made an outstanding start and frustrated Nottingham Forest twice in four days.

The England international secured his second successive clean sheet in this City Ground sequel to underline why Leeds moved to eclipse the previous record for Jordan Pickford.

“England’s No 1” was a frequent chant from the travelling Leeds fans and although it may take some time for him to dislodge Pickford as the country’s first-choice, he is loving life at his new club.

Trafford produced a number of fine saves and goals from Daniel James and James Justin secured a comfortable Carabao Cup second-round victory for Leeds, who also won here in the league on Saturday.

Dan James has put Leeds ahead against Nottingham Forest 💥 pic.twitter.com/BdiYMXFJ5h.

Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “He has the potential to be one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League and that is why Thomas Tuchel has picked him for England.

“I like his natural confidence and aura, he knows that he’s good and he will be outstanding one day.

“He has major chances to be under the spotlight and we are very pleased with him so far.”.

It has been revealed that forest manager Oliver Glasner will be pleased to see the back of Leeds. He was appointed by Forest for the primary reason of winning trophies after successful tenures with Crystal Palace and Eintracht Frankfurt, but this particular avenue is now closed for this season.

Four-time League Cup winners, Forest endured a difficult evening following the pre-match news that they have agreed a £45m deal with Chelsea for striker Liam Delap.

Industry observers note that forest have established a reputation for noisy transfer windows but are determined to focus on quality over quantity this year. With Delap to undergo a medical on Wednesday, Forest will then focus on signing a new right wing-back before the deadline.

Newcastle’s Jacob Murphy has been discussed, though a move is now regarded as unlikely. There are understood to be other targets under consideration.

Glasner has insisted he does not want Forest to panic, and it remains to be seen whether they do spring into life on the final day. He said: “I am not a magician or the messiah and we cannot ignore the reality that Leeds are ahead of us at the moment.

According to recent reports, “For nine months last season we were fighting relegation, so the players know it is going to take a lot of work. I know exactly what we have to change and that is what we will do.

In a recent development, “We are responsible and made so many mistakes. Maybe we needed this result. At the moment we are far away from what we want but we will get there.”.

This was a more open game than the attritional encounter from last weekend, as Trafford was forced into a fine early save to prevent Ola Aina’s cross from arcing into the top corner.

Yet both teams were frequently making mistakes and providing masterclasses in how to misplace passes, frustrating their respective managers in the technical area.

The most impressive moment of the first-half came from Leeds centre-back Joe Rodon, racing back into position to deny Chris Wood from close range. Rodon celebrated the tackle as if it were a 30-yard screamer.

It was always likely to be a mistake which proved the pivotal moment, and Arnaud Kalimuendo’s poor header cost the home team in the 50th minute.

Kalimuendo’s error presented Sean Longstaff with space to run into and his pass found James, who beat Matz Sels with a clinical finish.

“Can we play you every week?” was the inevitable chant from the travelling Leeds supporters.

Forest’s fans were becoming twitchy and Trafford produced another save to frustrate Wood from eight yards after a break down the right from Kalimuendo.

Glasner responded by making a quadruple substitution on the hour, yet Leeds remained dangerous and added a second goal 15 minutes from time when Justin bundled home after a goalmouth scramble.

In a recent development, ethan Ampadu's long throw causes CHAOS in the Forest box as Leeds go 2-0 up! pic.twitter.com/CtGDDIaRNp.

You can catch the draw for the next stage of the League Cup on Sky Sports Main Event tomorrow night after the conclusion of Preston North End vs Everton.

Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record deal worth £45m for Chelsea forward Liam Delap.

Delap has been deemed surplus to requirements at Stamford Bridge, and while the clubs were in talks over an initial loan deal, they have now struck a permanent agreement for the striker.

Sources indicate that the 23-year-old​ only signed for Chelsea in a £30m deal from Ipswich Town 12 months ago​ ​and is scheduled for a medical on Wednesday​. He will become Forest’s most expensive signing with the deal eclipsing the £37.5m they paid for Omari Hutchinson last summer.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a latest forward and Delap was a long-term target for the Austrian since his time as Crystal Palace head coach.

Delap held talks with Forest last year over a potential move, and was also understood to have spoken with Glasner while he was at Palace.

Speaking to ITV after the win, Rodon said: “I thought we were a bit sharper going forward, maybe a bit naive in the first half. I thought we had a lot of good chances maybe could have scored a couple of goals but we know it’s a difficult place to come and overall very happy to keep a clean sheet and win the game.”.

Of his last-ditch tackle in the first half, he added: “We love it, as defenders it’s as good as a goal. I’m delighted, [keeping] clean sheets is my job and overall I got it right in the end.”.

"There's a healthy arrogance about Leeds""Farke has gone from strength to strength"Izzy Christiansen and Jobi McAnuff praise the impact of Daniel Farke at Leeds 📈 pic.twitter.com/fgzLWRk3U2.

"It's a bit soon to say Wembley!" 😅James Justin and Dan James react to Leeds progressing into round three of the Carabao Cup 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/m81C6eJT7C.

Industry observers note that and that is it. Two home defeats by Leeds in less than 80 hours for Forest. Glasner will have much to ponder with a daunting trip to Anfield coming up on Saturday. All smiles for Farke’s side.

In a recent development, A look at a third for Leeds. Aaronson drives forward before setting Wilson who in turn lays on a first-time pass to Calvert-Lewin. The forward attempts to take his shot first time but can’t get the requisite power on the ball to beat Sels.

A pitch invader makes a brief appearance on the turf but is swiftly ushered away.

There is a late chance for Forest. Hutchinson’s cross is helped on by Dominguez but that touch inadvertently takes the ball away from Ndoye at the back post.

Forest fans are filing out of the exits and who can blame them?

There will be six minutes of added time.

That just about sums up Forest’s night. Dominguez stands over a free-kick from a dangerous area and, with the box loaded with their most imposing aerial threats, the midfielder sends the ball well over their heads and out for a goal-kick. So poor.

Calvert-Lewin is now on for Nmecha. Not really the striker Forest defenders would want to see at this stage of the game.

Another set-piece, this time a Stach corner, is barely dealt with by Forest.

There’s a shout for a handball at the other end as Ndoye spears a cross into the body of Elvedi, but the referee rightly waves the appeals away.

Recent findings suggest that the “oles” ring out from the away end as Leeds string a series of passes together in the corner right in front of it. Forest are looking rather helpless here.

Recent findings suggest that nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 2 (Justin) Ampadu introduces a throw-in from the right but has to reload as the referee notices some pushing in the box. His next attempt is far too loopy but causes Forest all sorts of trouble, bouncing and bobbling, and coming all the way through a thicket of limbs to Nmecha at the far post. Williams attempts to keep the ball out from a prone position on the goalline under pressure from Justin, who gets the final touch as the ball is bundled over the line.

It's messy but Leeds won't care! 😁Forest fail to deal with the throw-in and Nmecha is there to bundle it in...#EFL | #CarabaoCup pic.twitter.com/oV46fs5RmP.

Jair goes into the book after catching Ampadu in full flight. He never had a prayer of reaching that ball.

The resulting free-kick lands to Amapadu himself in the box, but his effort is deflected behind for a corner which is not up to much.

Goalscorer James is taken off for Bogle, who will offer more mettle down Leeds’ right side as Forest search for an equaliser in the closing stages.

In a recent development, stach has only been on the field for a matter of seconds but comes within a few inches of scoring. Wilson does well on the edge of the box before laying the ball to Stach whose curled effort grazes the outside of the side-netting.

Longstaff’s final contribution to this game is a foul and yellow card as he spreads his legs wide to stop Ndoye breaking away through the middle.

He is replaced by Wilson, as Tanaka and Okafaor also make way, for Stach and Aaronson.

It has been revealed that there’s plenty more endeavour down Forest’s upcoming-look left side. Hudson Odoi scampers down that flank before cutting inside, and while he’s unable to fashion a chance the intent is correct.

Industry observers note that the substitutions appear to have breathed life into this Forest side. Murillo picks out Dominguez charging forward and Trafford does well to tip the midfielder’s effort behind. The resulting corner comes to nothing.

Glasner resolves he has seen enough and rings the changes. Diomande, Aina, Jesus and Kalimuendo are replaced by Murillo, Netz, Ndoye and Hudson Odoi.

Okafor indicates off his dancing feet in the Forest box, pulling off a few stepovers before the ball comes to Ampadu on the edge of the area but his strike is dragged wide.

Chances at both ends! Kalimuendo plays a wonderful ball into the box for Wood to sweep home but Trafford springs into action and makes a stunning save.

Leeds go up the other end, Okafor profiting from a diversionary run from centre-back Elvedi but cannot find the target and double Forest’s lead.

Leeds are ahead and the inevitable chant from the away supporters is “can we play you every week?”.

This is of course their second meeting in four days and Leeds are on course to record the double.

Forest’s fans are starting to get a little twitchy.

Dan James puts Leeds United in front! ⚽️Tidy finish from the Welshman... #EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/GzWg6zLGLm.

It has been revealed that nottingham Forest 0 Leeds United 1 (James) We finally have a breakthrough. Kalimuendo gives the ball up cheaply in the middle of the park and Longstaff is there to pick up the pieces, darting infield before laying on a perfectly weighted for James to gallop on to, take a touch and sweep beyond Sels. The winger has been Leeds’ biggest threat and deserves that goal.

James finds space down the right - again - and his cross is closed down and deflected behind for a corner.

Longstaff’s floated delivery is tipped away by Sels, but it turns out that the ball went out before coming in so a Forest goal kick is awarded.

A lovely rendition of Mull of Kintyre precedes a short blast of the referee’s whistle and we’re back under way...

Schlager goes into the book instantly for grabbing a handful of Tanaka’s shirt as the Japan international attempted to escape his clutches.

This hasn’t been much of an improvement from Saturday.

Recent findings suggest that both teams are producing masterclasses in how to misplace passes. Oliver Glasner and Daniel Farke have spent much of the first half looking very frustrated.

James Trafford must be feeling very comfortable and confident of a second successive clean sheet after joining from Manchester City.

Let’s hope for an improvement in the second-half.

Industry observers note that should the scores remain level after 90 minutes, we will go straight to penalties. There’s still a half to play of course, but Forest’s League Cup shoot-out record should be a source of confidence having won seven from eight.

Leeds have only won four from 10.

What a tackle from Joe Rodon! 💥#EFL | #CarabaoCup | @LUFC pic.twitter.com/p5GkzSFEoZ.

Recent findings suggest that james wins the ball on the halfway line and feeds Okafor down the left. He attempts a deft through-ball into a thicket of bodies but it comes to nothing.

Leeds circulate the ball, working the ball from side to side but there is nowhere near enough movement in front of the ball-player for any meaningful forward passes to be played.

And, quite aptly, the referee blows up at three seconds past 45 minutes. Certainly not a half for the books.

Another half-chance for Forest! Milenkovic lands on a second ball off a deep free-kick but he cannot keep his strike down. A classic centre-half’s effort if you will.

Elvedi and Muharemovic look to be astute buys from Leeds’ perspective. Both assured at the back and the latter especially is confident progressing the ball.

Just as I type that Forest threaten with a ball over the top, but Justin nips in to take the ball away from Wood.

Another decent opening for Leeds after a Forest turnover. Nmecha strides through the middle but Milenkovic is in position to ensure his run comes to nothing.

Recent findings suggest that what a tackle! Kalimuendo bursts through the middle after Leeds cede possession in a dangerous position. The winger plays in Wood who looks to be through on goal but Rodon comes out of nowhere to telescope a limb and stop the forward in his tracks. Fantastic defensive work from the Welshman.

It’s then Okafor’s turn to put in a dangerous cross from the left, but Nmecha cannot get to it.

Tanaka becomes the first man to go into the book. The ball gets away from him and Jesus puts body between man and ball smartly to win the foul.

Sources indicate that tanaka is now dropping into the back line to allow Leeds’ defenders the licence to get wider and higher. Forest will need to be wary of their opponents’ numerical advantage down the flanks.

Tanaka then turns provider, winning possession in Forest’s half before playing in Longstaff, whose cross-cum-shot does not threaten Sels’ goal.

Dominguez stands up a smart cross to the far post where Aina is waiting to head back across goal. Trafford backpedals into Kalimuendo and the referee awards Leeds a free-kick.

Wonderful touch there early in the game from none other than Oliver Glasner.

Forest’s head coach perfectly trapped a high ball as it landed towards him in the technical area.

James demonstrates off his speed for the first time tonight, accelerating down the right before fizzing a dangerous ball into the six-yard box but Forest clear their lines.

Forest are in their red home shirts, kicking from left to right. Leeds are in their yellow away number. Same set-up as the weekend.

Sources indicate that players and mascots walk on to the City Ground turf. A place in the League Cup third round on the line.

Reflecting on Saturday’s defeat by Leeds in his programme notes, Glasner wrote: “I saw plenty of encouraging signs from the team on Saturday and I felt we were a lot closer to scoring than we were conceding, especially in the second half. Unfortunately, the small margins were not on our side.

“I thought our defence looked comfortable, but there is still work to be done and the more the players get used to the system we’re operating, the more we’ll see that work come to fruition in competitive matches.

“We have recovered well and will be ready to give our all this evening.”.

Previewing tonight’s League Cup match, Leeds head coach Daniel Farke said: “Our league win is good for our mood and confidence, but this is a ‘do or die’ cup game. Both teams will be motivated to progress, so I expect a tight game. It will be difficult to win on the road again against a tough opponent.”.

Sources indicate that when asked what winning a first trophy of his managerial career would mean to him, Farke added: “Well, we weren’t too far away last season. Overall, I would say my form in cup competitions hasn’t been too bad during my career. I’m a massive believer in these competitions, I like the ‘do or die’ mentality. I would never say no to another good cup run.”.

The hosts’ kits tonight will include Carabao Cup sleeve patches with the number four on them, in recognition of the club’s League Cup triumphs in 1978, 1979, 1989 and 1990.

Daniel Farke ruined the Oliver Glasner welcoming party on Saturday with a 1-0 smash-and-grab victory at the death.

Both managers have gone relatively strong for this tie, with only a sprinkling of debuts.

Ousmane Diomande, the £34m signing from Sporting, makes his first appearance while there is a first start for Xaver Schlager.

The big breaking news is that Forest are smashing their club record to sign Chelsea forward Liam Delap for £45m.

Delap will undergo a medical at Forest on Wednesday with the deal potentially rising to £50m after add-ons.

It eclipses the previous transfer record of £37.5m for winger Omari Hutchinson.

Oliver Glasner has prioritised the addition of a latest centre-forward this summer and Delap ticks pretty much every box for him.

Farke makes six changes to the complement that started against Forest in the league on Saturday.

Welcome to live coverage of the Carabao Cup second-round match between Nottingham Forest and Leeds United. This will be the sides’ second meeting at the City Ground in four days after Anton Stach’s late free-kick decided an attritional contest on the Premier League’s opening weekend. Forest’s newly introduced head coach Oliver Glasner is something of a cup specialist, though, with FA Cup, Europa League and Conference League titles to his name and he will relish the opportunity to right the wrongs of Saturday in front of the Forest faithful.

The Austrian is Forest’s fifth head coach in less than 12 months and he will look to arrest the churn by bringing to the City Ground the success he enjoyed with Crystal Palace. During pre-season, the Austrian moulded Forest into his preferred 3-4-3 shape, placing summer acquisition Ousmane Diomande alongside the existing central-defensive partnership of Murillo and Nikola Milenković. Here, Diomande gets his Forest debut and Glasner brings in talisman Chris Wood from the start.

Recent findings suggest that daniel Farke will have been delighted to see his Leeds side continue their excellent form in pre-season – which included victories over Liverpool, Red Bull Leipzig and Augsburg – into the season proper. Although Leeds arrive at the City Ground shorn of attacking options Wilfried Gnonto, Noah Okafor and Mateo Joseph through injury, Farke still shuffles the pack in the forward positions with this weekend’s visit of Brentford to Elland Road in mind.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vous avez pu suivre cette rencontre en direct sur notre forum grâce à notre envoyé spécial MachuPicchu42 : les U17 ont concédé un match nul et vierge à la mi-journée face au Cavigal de Nice au Stade Georges Bereta du Centre Robert Herbin.

Recent findings suggest that dominateurs jusqu'à l'entame du dernier quart d'heure, les Verts ont eu deux grosses occasions en première période. Sur la première, le portier niçois a repoussé le tir à bout portant de Naël Dani. Sur la seconde, un défenseur visiteur a repoussé sur sa ligne une tête d'Isaak Seydi (photo).

According to recent reports, en deuxième mi-temps, Lohoré Gobé a eu à son tour une belle opportunité d'ouvrir le score mais sa tentative a été déjouée par le gardien azuréen. Isaak Seydi a de nouveau eu une occase de la tête, hélas non cadrée. Izaya Kimpioka a raté un face à face en tirant à côté. Les visteurs se sont enhardis lors de 20 dernières minutes pas très bien maîtrisées par les Stéphanois mais Andra Laugier n'aura eu aucun arrêt à faire de toute la rencontre.

L'ASSE a perdu sa 5e place au profit de son ex-club partenaire Saint-Priest, qui a cartonné 6-1 le Gazelec Ajaccio (avant-dernier), prochain adversaire des Verts (dimanche prochain en Corse).

La compo : Laugier - Tiambo (Balta, 33') - Mnemoi, Dagbo, Bufferne - Demassieux, Mendy (Thibaudat, 77'), Gobé - Seydi, Kimpioka, Dani (Aytone, 70').

In a recent development, la réaction de David Le Moal : "On a eu la mainmise sur le match jusqu'au dernier quart d'heure. On a eu pas mal d'occasions, c'est dommage qu'on n'ait pas réussi à les convertir. En première période, on a eu du mal à passer l'adversaire dans le coeur du jeu donc on s'est évertué à contourner le bloc assez bas du Cavigal. On a eu plein de situations de centres mais on a manqué de réalisme dans le dernier geste ou dans l'avant-dernier geste. On a eu plusieurs occasions assez nettes en première période comme en seconde. Je n'ai pas trop compris pourquoi on a reculé lors du dernier quart d'heure, nos adversaires ont eu quelques opportunités en fin de match. Je suis un peu déçu qu'on n'ait pas réussi à marquer mais je suis assez content des vrais gestes défensifs et de la discipline tactique, on a laissé très peu de situations à l'adversaire.".

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

A late equaliser for Fortuna Sittard in De Kuip proved costly for Feyenoord as PSV and Twente racked up huge victories to move within two points of the Eredivisie leaders.

Feyenoord paid the price for failing to finish off the Limburgers, with Luciano Valente’s 59th-minute goal the only reward for their dominance.

Fortuna equalised with four minutes left when Shiloh ’t Zand, on loan from Feyenoord, was allowed to run through to the penalty area and beat Tjark Ernst with a low shot.

In a recent development, feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst made no effort to hide his disappointment. “We know that Fortuna are the kind of team who can score from the few attacks they have,” he noted. “If you don’t score the goals, things like this can happen.”.

Second-placed Ajax are a point behind after a narrow win at home against AZ ended an 11-match winless streak against the Alkmaar club, as Tolu Arokodare’s early header proved decisive.

Twente recorded the biggest win of the weekend with a 9-0 demolition of Excelsior in Rotterdam, with Wout Weghorst scoring four times and Sondre Ørjasaeter notching up five assists.

In a recent development, excelsior collapsed following the fifth-minute dismissal of Nesto Groen for a reckless high challenge. The home side were 5-0 down at half-time, with Weghorst claiming a hat-trick in the opening 33 minutes.

PSV bagged seven goals in a one-sided encounter with bottom club Willem II, with all the goals coming from different scorers including Ricardo Pepi, who came on in the second half after a six-week absence through injury.

Telstar opened up a three-point gap at the bottom over ADO Den Haag with a 4-2 win against Utrecht in a painful return to Velsen-Zuid for Telstar’s former coach Anthony Correia.

ADO went down 1-0 in Zwolle, with PEC’s Dylan Mbayo scoring the only goal with a first-time finish on the stroke of half-time.

The match between Cambuur Leeuwarden and Go Ahead Eagles was suspended in the 82nd minute after visiting fans threw fireworks onto the pitch.

The clubs agreed with the KNVB not to play the final minutes and allow Cambuur’s 4-0 advantage to stand as the final result.

Go Ahead’s director Jan-Willem van Dop mentioned the club would take action against those responsible: “I am ashamed on behalf a small group of supporters who ruined things for the club and a large hare of the fans in the away end,” he said.

Cambuur Leeuwarden 4-0 Go Ahead Eagles.

Le parole di Abate nel post-partita con il Napoli accendono i riflettori sulle condizioni di Belghali e Ismajli verso la sfida contro i biancocelesti; stop muscolare pure per Biraghi.

In vista della sfida di sabato 28 novembre alle 18:00, valida per la 13ª giornata di Serie A, che vedrà i biancocelesti impegnati nella trasferta sul campo del Torino, le condizioni fisiche in casa granata assumono un peso specifico notevole per la Lazio, chiamata a guardare con attenzione alle possibili assenze emerse dopo la gara con il Napoli.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

It has been revealed that al termine della partita di ieri sera contro i partenopei, il tecnico Abate ha fatto chiarezza sulle condizioni di due elementi della rosa: "Belghali si porta dietro un problema al ginocchio da settimane, Ismajli potrebbe essersi rotto un dito della mano". Due situazioni da valutare giorno per giorno che interessano da vicino anche la Lazio: Belghali stava attraversando un ottimo momento di forma prima dello stop, mentre Ismajli si è fin qui dimostrato il più affidabile e brillante del terzetto difensivo granata. La loro assenza sarebbe un duro colpo per il Torino nella sfida contro i biancocelesti.

Sources indicate that sempre dopo la sfida con il Napoli, l'allenatore granata ha aggiunto un ulteriore aggiornamento chiave per la preparazione della Lazio: "Biraghi ha avuto un affaticamento". Un problema muscolare che impone cautela in settimana per evitare ricadute e che mette a rischio la sua presenza per la 13ª giornata di campionato, togliendo potenzialmente esperienza e spinta sulla fascia ai granata nel confronto con i biancocelesti.

As part of PortuGOAL’s efforts to constantly evolve and serve lovers of Portuguese football with top-quality and increasingly accessible content, we are replacing the PortuGOAL Android and Apple APPs with a newly introduced Progressive Web Application (PWA) as from tomorrow, Tuesday 3 April.

Sources indicate that this big step forward in phone apps technology loads the content instantly, even in areas of low connectivity, stays up to date at all times, displays the most recent version upon launching, is more efficient than native apps, works on-demand and is always accessible, without taking up a smartphone’s valuable memory or data. In a recent development, in another improvement, the website itself will be implementing SSL technology at the same time, leading to more secure and faster navigation. PortuGOAListas should be directed to the new URL automatically from tomorrow, if not simply type http://portugoal.net into your browser’s address bar then bookmark the page. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Noham Akil, buteur après son entrée en jeu.

Ayant mis fin le week-end dernier à une série de 5 défaites consécutives, les U19 de Frédéric Dugand, victorieux à domicile du Cap d’Ail (2-1) se déplaçaient à Nice ce dimanche, pour y affronter le très bon club formateur du Cavigal. Une victoire sur la Côte d’Azur permettait aux jeunes Verts de rejoindre son adversaire au classement (13 points).

Sous une légère pluie, dans un stade Bob Rémond, du nom du formateur Niçois, aussi appelé « père spirituel de Robert Herbin », les Stéphanois, réduits à 10 et menés au score ont été cherché l’égalisation en toute fin de rencontre (1-1).

Sources indicate that en première période les Verts, avec notamment Noa Moulin, habituellement aligné en réserve, sont bien en place et disciplinés mais restent un peu timides dans leurs actions pour espérer peser davantage sur la rencontre. A la 23ème minute, consécutivement à un corner adverse mal repoussé, le ballon arrive au second poteau, est remis dans la surface verte et repris par un niçois qui vient tromper Mael Massé pour l’ouverture du score. (Cavigal Nice 1 - ASSE 0 ; mi-temps).

Au retour des vestiaires, les Stéphanois plus entreprenants vont chercher l’adversaire plus haut. Progressivement, les contres deviennent verts et la confiance revient. Pourtant à l’heure de jeu, la situation se complique, Tidiane Vibert est exclu pour un geste d’humeur et laisse ses coéquipiers en infériorité numérique. Touchés, mais pas coulés, les Stéphanois, sous l’impulsion notamment de l’entrant Medhy Lutin Zidee à la 56ème continuent à faire bloc et à jouer les coups à fond. Leurs efforts vont être récompensés, à la 84ème minute,  Maxime Lengué Lenou trouve Noham Akil (entré quelques minutes plus tôt) qui du pied droit vient ajuster le portier azuréen. Les Verts sont décomplexés et tiennent ce point précieux qui les voit enchainer une seconde rencontre consécutive sans perdre.

(Cavigal Nice 1 - ASSE 1 ; score final).

Après ce partage des points, les Stéphanois auront la semaine prochaine l’occasion de poursuivre leur série dans leur quête de points pour assurer le maintien avec la réception du  Gazelec Ajaccio, auteur d’un nul aujourd’hui face à Balma (1-1) et comptant le même nombre de points que les Verts, mais un match en moins..

La Composition : Massé  – Lengi (Assoumani 81ème),  E.Mnemoi, N.Mouton, Jolivet, Lengue Lenou– Vibert, Thouilleux (Akil 76ème), Moulin (Gary 56ème), Marliac(Lutin Zidee 56ème) - Zibi.

Recent findings suggest that la réaction de Frédéric Dugand : « Je suis satisfait du résultat, de la capacité du groupe à avoir respecté le blueprint de jeu décidé, un peu plus prudent qu’à l’habitude. On fait une bonne seconde période, les joueurs ont eu du répondant. J’ai vu un groupe « habité »des joueurs qui se sont parlé et qui ont été acteurs du match. Le groupe se transforme, il faut capitaliser sur cette attitude, tâcher maintenant d’avoir cette mentalité dès le coup d’envoi, pour aller chercher des émotions ensemble .On peut et on doit aller encore plus loin dans l’investissement et dans la prise de conscience de nos possibilités. ».

Top five football betting tips and tricks

📅 31 Aug 2018 | ⏱️ 4 min read (795 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Portugoal

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well.
  • Getting started on football betting is far from easy, though.
  • It has been revealed that but experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well. Especially popular in Europe, betting on football can be an incredibly profitable enterprise, so long as you know how to do it.

Getting started on football betting is far from easy, though. This form of gambling requires dedication, investment, and persistence. As you gain experience, your intuition will improve and you will be able to make more correct predictions.

It has been revealed that but experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter. In fact, you can substantially improve your betting strategy by simply following some basic football betting tips.

Industry observers note that you might find shopping around boring and unhelpful, but you just have to do it when you search sites for football betting. As you know, the higher the odds, the bigger the payout. What you may have missed, however, is that odds are different at each bookmaker. Having remarked that, shopping around for the best odds is sensible, as it rewards you with bigger payouts.

Industry observers note that in this line of thought, sticking to one bookmaker is virtually pointless. Even if the bookie of your choosing offers the best odds for a number of matches, it is highly unlikely that their odds will remain the best for long.

According to recent reports, an obvious one, we know. And yet, you will be surprised by the number of football bettors who wager on football, but do not follow the sport. So, why is it notable to follow the action closely?

First of all, by watching football matches, you can take part in the most exciting football betting market – the live betting market. What is more crucial, however, is that following the action provides an invaluable insight into teams and players’ style, condition, and determination – important factors  to consider when placing a bet.

Recent findings suggest that as you watch more and more games, you will improve your analytic abilities. In time, you will be able to make more accurate predictions about the outcome of different matches, which, of course,  will result in placing more winning bets.

Recent findings suggest that as you know, odds are based on the probability of occurrence of a certain outcome; the higher the odds, the more unlikely it is for that outcome to actually occur. But what happens when the odds offered by the bookmaker represent a probability that is lower than the actual probability of an outcome occurring? In such a situation, you can place what is called a value bet.

If you want to become a professional football punter, you should always search for value when betting, as it leads to huge profits.

Favoured by beginners in particular, accumulators are a type of football wager which allows you to bet on as many fixtures as you like. Most commonly, you will be asked to choose a match winner, but as the market is diverse, you may be offered a number of other betting options. What makes accumulators an appealing betting market is the huge potential payout – here, you can stake as little as £1 and have the potential to win more than £500,000, depending on the bookmaker and the number of selected fixtures.

It has been revealed that if you find accumulators’ payouts too good to be true, you are right. As a matter of fact, there is a reason for the odds to be set so high – actually winning an accumulator bet, especially one which involves a wide selection of matches, is nearly impossible. You see, all you need for your whole wager to lose is one wrong prediction. For example, if you bet on 10 matches and just one of them goes wrong, your entire accumulator is lost.

To make money by betting on football, avoid betting on accumulators – the risk is simply not worth it.

Industry observers note that finally, if you want to be a successful football punter, learn how not to mix emotions with betting. This is easier remarked than done, though.

Whenever your favourite team plays, you want them to win, regardless of how (im)possible that may be. If you do not learn how to leave emotions out of betting, however, you are highly likely to put money on your favourite team even if they have no chance of winning the match. Conversely, should you base your bets on hard facts and not on emotions, you increase your chances to win.

Our advice – avoid betting on fixtures that involve one of your favourite teams, that is the easiest way to keep emotions at bay.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest significant-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his newly introduced club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”.

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX.

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

Recent findings suggest that in the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs.

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi mentioned. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”.

Recent findings suggest that cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Recent findings suggest that buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”.

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Industry observers note that the victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

“Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against massive teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”.

A place in the League Cup third round is at stake as Tottenham host Charlton in a London derby at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a substantial player for us.

Recent findings suggest that “I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”.

Industry observers note that omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones noted. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most key.”.

Dual passports issue continues to plague Dutch-based footballers

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.

Suriname’s parliament passed a law in September enabling players who are selected for the national team to gain citizenship automatically.

But the Dutch immigration service IND remarked the law passed in Suriname made no difference to the rules on dual nationality in the Netherlands.

“The fact that Surinamese nationality has been obtained by legal means is not enough on its own to qualify for one of the exceptional categories under our law,” a spokesman for the Dutch justice ministry told broadcaster NOS.

The law was intended to settle the question of dual nationality for footballers, which arose last March when NAC Breda challenged the eligibility of Go Ahead Eagles defender Dean James.

James took Indonesian citizenship last year after accepting an invitation to play for the national team, but under Dutch dual nationality rules he was required to give up his original passport.

The Dutch football association KNVB debuted an investigation into the employment status of players who were called up by countries such as Suriname, Cape Verde and Indonesia. In the meantime it arranged for Dutch-based players to be given temporary work permits so they could keep playing for their clubs.

Losing Dutch nationality also stripped them of their EU citizenship, meaning they would need to obtain visas and meet stricter criteria, such as an annual salary threshold of €600,000, to be eligible to play in the Eredivisie.

Several players have passed up invitations to join the Surinamese squad because of the uncertainty, including Danilho Doekhi of Lazio, Milan van Ewijk of Coventry City and Jayden Oosterwolde of Fenerbahçe.

National team manager Henk Fraser stated it was “inexplicable” that players’ livelihoods were being damaged by their desire to play international football.

“Both countries have to get together and clarify the situation,” he told NOS. “This is a straightforward case of people following their hearts and wanting to play for Suriname, but not knowing where they stand.”.

Some players noted they felt misled by the Surinamese football association, which told them they were playing for the national team on “sports passports” that allowed them to remain Dutch citizens.

Former Feyenoord winger Jean-Paul Boëtius noted he only discovered after he was first called up for Suriname last year that he had inadvertently renounced his Dutch citizenship as a result.

Shortly afterwards he received a letter from the city council in Rotterdam telling him to hand in his Dutch passport, which he had recently renewed, because it was no longer valid.

Industry observers note that “I now have a sticker in my Surinamese passport that says I have a residency permit allowing me to live in the Netherlands,” he told NOS. “But that’s only for a year. It’s a very difficult situation. I want to become Dutch again. I was born and brought up here.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vous avez pu suivre la rencontre de cet après-midi en direct sur la chaîne YouTube de l'ASSE : à Aimé Jacquet, la réserve a logiquement battu 2-0 le Stade Beaucairois FC (lanterne rouge n'ayant pris que 2 petits points depuis le début de la saison de N2).

Recent findings suggest that dominateurs, les Verts ont péché dans la finition lors d'une première période qui a beaucoup penché à gauche avec l'association de deux joueurs dénichés à l'Institut Diambars (Sénégal) : le revenant Lassana Traoré (qui n'avait plus joué depuis 14 mois !) et le très prometteur ailier d'un an son cadet Etienne Mendy (photo), encore dans tous les bons coups ce dimanche. Ce dernier, à l'instar de Niels Rised, a eu l'occasion d'ouvrir le score en première période mais sa frappe trop écrasée a été arrêtée par le portier gardois. Suite à une énième percussion, il a délivré un centre parfait pour son capitaine Adam Baallal dont la tête n'a pas trouvé le cadre.

Deux minutes après le retour des vestiaires, les Verts ont fait sauter le verrou de Beaucaire sur un corner parfaitement tiré par Lucas Reynaud et repris magistralement par Mourtada Gueye d'une tête décroisée imparable. Obligés de courir après le score, les visiteurs ont laissé pas mal d'espace aux Verts, qui ont parfois confondu vitesse et précipitation au moment de porter l'estocade. Heureusement l'intenable Etienne Mendy a inscrit le but du break à la 82e d'un lob magistral de 47 mètres et Sainté a su parfaitement gérer la fin de match.

🙂‍↔️ Le lob de 50 mètres d'Étienne Mendy pour valider le succès de la Réserve ! https://t.co/P4pgjzieZI.

Les Verts consolident leur place sur le podium à 4 longueurs du leader Berre (battu par la réserve de l'OM) et à 3 points de l'Atlas Paillade, qui reste sur une série de 6 succès avant de recevoir l'ASSE lors de la prochaine journée, le samedi 5 décembre à 18h00. Une belle affiche en perspective à suivre sur Poteaux Carrés juste avant le choc au sommet de la 14e journée de L2 entre les leaders stéphanois et leurs dauphins nancéiens !

La compo : Colombet - Teillol, Gueye, Kasia, L.Traoré (Benkou, 46') - Depalle (A.Traoré, 69'), Baallal, Rised - Reynaud, Paalberg (Toty, 73'), E.Mendy.

La réaction de Sylvain Gibert :.

According to recent reports, "On est satisfait d'avoir enchaîné un 3e succès consécutif. C'était un math un peu piégeux au vu du classement de nos adversaires. J'avais donc mis en garde nos joueurs car Beaucaire avait perdu cette saison des matches qu'il ne méritait pas de perdre. J'avais vraiment alerté le groupe, lui avait demandé d'être rigoureux. On fait une bonne première demi-heure sans concrétiser, on a un peu déjoué le dernier quart d'heure de le première période, on a alors commis des fautes un peu bêtes, on a concédé des coups francs hereusement sans conséquence.

In a recent development, le mot d'ordre à la mi-temps c'était de rester calmes, de continuer de jouer pour gagner à l'usure. Notre rapide ouverture du score en seconde période nous a facilité le travail. Je suis content qu'on ait ouvert le score sur coup de pied arrêté, on sait que ça permet parfois de décanter des matches. On bosse beaucoup là-dessus, Haïdar [Al-Shaïbani, entraîneur des gardiens, ndp2 et responsable des cpa, ndp2] en particulier. Le match a alors été plus ouvert car Beaucaire a dû un peu se découvrir pour tenter d'égaliser.

Etienne a fait parler son talent, il a mis un top but, un lob de près de 50 mètres du gauche alors que c'est un droitier. J'ai bien aimé l'état d'esprit des mecs, même à 2-0 on ne s'est pas relâché, on a continué d'attaquer et surtout de ne pas prendre de but. Cette victoire vient une fois de plus récompenser tout le boulot des joueurs. Vraiment, ça fait plaisir de coacher une vraie équipe, l'état d'esprit de tous les joueurs, notamment celui d'Adam qui a fait un très bon match au milieu. Tout le monde esst concerné, c'est appréciable !".

Feyenoord are facing a heavy fine from European football authorities after fireworks were let off during their Champions League defeat by Internazionale.

It has been revealed that referee Glenn Nyberg suspended the match for several minutes after flares were fired onto the roof from outside De Kuip stadium, damaging the structure. Police later made two arrests.

“It’s obviously not right and it’ll be another fine,” coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst said wearily after the game, which ended in a comprehensive 3-0 defeat for his team.

Sources indicate that one flare landed on the pitch despite the club taking measures such as hanging nets from the gantries to stop objects being thrown from the stands. “They’re letting off fireworks from outside now,” Van Bronckhorst noted. “What do you do about that?”.

Uefa are likely to hit Feyenoord with a fine and could order the club to close parts of the stadium for their next home matches in the competition, against Porto on November 24 and RB Leipzig on January 27.

The club also have a suspended penalty hanging over them from last October, when they were fined €60,000 after fans let off fireworks during the match against Greek club Panathinaikos.

On the pitch, Feyenoord were undone by a classic display of Italian defending and counter-attacking, as Internazionale sat back after taking an eighth-minute lead through Yann Bisseck.

Francesco Pio Esposito headed in a second early in the second half, just as Feyenoord were pushing for an equaliser, before Piotr Zielinski made sure of the win with a shot from 20 metres.

Captain Luciano Valente stated the result was “more than deserved” and the visitors had shown more “quality”.

“This defeat was harder to take than the one against Barcelona,” he told Ziggo Sport. “Because we thought going in that we could get something, but we just weren’t good enough.”.

In a recent development, van Bronckhorst said he was not surprised by the difference in class between the teams. “They scored the first goal out of nothing,” he said. “And Inter know better what the game needs at every stage.

It has been revealed that “Their players have a lot of experience, they’ve been in the final twice in the last four years. So we’re at a disadvantage.”.

#164634. Opinion: The morality of football

Opinion: The morality of football

📅 08 Jun 2023 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1297 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Portugoal

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.
  • That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.
  • Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yesterday evening, Selecao correspondent Nathan Motz accepted a unique opportunity to appear as a guest on the Moral Maze – a BBC radio broadcast dealing with matters of moral and ethical significance.

Is football a moral force for good? That was the question of the day, and each of the four guests were asked to discuss various aspects of the debate from financial fairplay to club takeovers by foreign entities to racism.

Nathan’s segment was concerned with whether football has transcendent moral value, and what that is exactly. Is there a greater significance to the game we are watching, or is it merely 22 humans kicking a leather ball into a net?

Join Nathan as he elaborates on the most significant takeaways of what was a fascinating discussion on the sport and morality in general.

Football, for some, may be the most poignant reminder of the moral universe in which we live. While debate has raged for centuries regarding the precise origin of moral absolutes and how humans ought to live, it is simply unavoidable to say humanity is often troubled by events surrounding the game we all love so dearly.

In not so distant history, every normal act of human life would have been assigned some degree of moral significance. Every action had inherently moral indicators - for good or for evil. Today, postmodern views of morality dominate. These describe morality as an entirely subjective dimension. In other words, it cannot be pinned down exactly whether behaviors are objectively good or bad. We can only find fault with someone else’s interpretation based on their own unique moral code. Morality is relative to the individual or society.

According to recent reports, yet last night’s dialogue concerning football and human behavior was filled with moral accusations and claims which strongly suggested humans are not content with relativist morality. Indeed, we are at times frightened by and disgusted with what we observe in and around football. Our sense of moral justice is deeply disturbed. But with respect to what exactly?

In responding to the panelist’s questions, I observed a familiar paradigm. Each time I have discussed any aspect of moral behavior, the speculation humans are good or at worst morally neutral animals continually reemerges. This widely accepted presupposition is then followed shortly by disgust at some aspect of human behavior. Almost as if to ask “why are all these good humans behaving so badly?” while ignoring the very real implications of this line of inquiry. A question rendered unanswerable by the insistent a priori assumptions from which it was derived.

In a recent development, if humans are intrinsically beneficent, conscientious, fair, humble, and honest then why is football rife with racism, misogyny, greed, disenfranchisement, lies, cheating, violence, and the hypocrisy to deny the occurrence of any such behaviors except when a rival club is the guilty party? Behaviors which are perpetrated by individual supporters, fanatical groups, club administrations, corporate bodies such as FIFA, political entities, nations, and even the players themselves. No one participating faction is guiltless.

It has been revealed that to so blithely sidestep more sufficient explanations for the empirical reality of wickedness in football and in human behavior more generally is not just factually incorrect. It undermines real attempts to understand the root of these behaviors where they might be dealt with more effectively.

To listen to The Moral Maze episode entitled “Football: a moral force for good?” produced by BBC radio and featuring PortuGOAL’s Seleção correspondent Nathan Motz click on this link.

Industry observers note that furthermore, in good faith, how successful is a response against heinous evil when those perpetrating it are regarded as behaving in accord with their unique moral ambitions? Humans refuse to accept their indisputably objective moral lacking at a fundamental level. This restricts us from ever doing any more than “stamping out” the alleged impropriety of others – while we ourselves may readily engage in these very same behaviors. Moral relativism cannot account for the moral outrage emanating from all corners of the football world. Is Qatar wrong to perpetrate human rights atrocities or is it allowable because their culture is indifferent? Is hooliganism objectively wrong, or only when someone else’s club is responsible?

It has been revealed that the overlooking of our own failings while lashing out at others for theirs is quintessential to the morally fallen nature of humanity itself. Football tells all. There are not good people and bad people. There are only people who both willfully and unintentionally transgress the moral code embedded in each of our hearts. A moral law which can only have ever been given by a moral Lawgiver. Otherwise, it is truly your word against mine as it pertains to the moral validity of all behaviors - even those which may deeply violate your conscience.

Industry observers note that football generates an episodic, semantic, and imagistic description of universal archetypes: good and evil, sacrifice and greed, cruelty and mercy, hero and anti-hero. It speaks to every arc of life’s plotline: tragedy, comedy, victory, defeat, the finite nature of our circumstances. It is one of the preeminent existential dialects alongside religion, visual art, written and spoken language, music, and theatre. Football plucks a primal chord.

As metaphysics have been curtailed to just physics in the modern secular West, football has only elevated our awareness of the often dire moral predicaments of our species. Yet it is clear the moral conversation does not originate on a football pitch. The pitch is but a grand stage upon which moral themes may be observed and critiqued, a mirror held in front of our own soul.

Sources indicate that the desire for ultimate purpose, for meaning beyond the material realm, never disappeared in modernity. Arguably, it has only become more desperate as the outcry for ultimate significance comes under more scrutiny and criticism by those who constrain ontological explanations to those accounted for by physics. The severity of the mental health crisis in the West is in no small part explained by the terrifying existential awareness we are cut adrift in an abstract sea of meaningless, hopeless wandering between two oblivions - that before mortal life began and that at mortal life’s end. Let football be one voice which reassures you - there is ultimate meaning and good reasons why football so unsettles our craving for justice.

It has been revealed that in a palpable, unavoidable way, football and supporter communities across Europe are encountering moral quandaries. In Portugal, age-old debates between FC Porto and Benfica have routinely been haunted by, in many cases, farcical and cynical hypocrisy. Throughout its history, the FPF has been susceptible to showing partiality to a club, player, or style which ultimately degrades the performance of our beloved Seleção. Deny it all we like, and not one aspect of this reality is changed.

It has been revealed that in conclusion, whatever your thoughts or beliefs on the subject of moral significance, its origin, the meaning of life, and how football draws that out, I hope it will be beneficial to examine these matters more deeply. In my zeal, I admit I have not always been prudent to initiate these discussions in a way which respects thoughtful disagreement. It is my hope this effort to bring that discussion to Portuguese football will be well-received and carefully pondered. But I will contentedly listen to those followers who may be genuinely unhappy or unsupportive of this or any other idea about which I write.

Sources indicate that the readers of this website and the larger Portuguese football loving world are my people. It is a joy and a responsibility I take seriously whenever I have the opportunity to raise key questions about the Selecao, the game, and our lives in general.

Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

Other reunions from Thursday’s draw include Manchester City travelling to Barcelona, to whom they last week sold Rodri, and Liverpool visiting Inter Milan, who have signed Curtis Jones.

Arsenal will also travel to Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich, while United will host the Germans as well on their Champions League return in a repeat of the legendary 1999 final. Michael Carrick’s side will also visit Cesc Fàbregas’s Como.

Mourinho last managed at the Emirates Stadium in March 2021, barely a month before his sacking by Spurs.

During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

Facing Kane in Munich does not seem any easier. Some tough assignments here including a trip to Napoli but the pot-four teams seem straightforward for Mikel Arteta.

PSV Eindhoven endured a frustrating night in the Champions League as their defensive frailties were exposed in a 2-1 defeat by Club Brugge.

PSV started full of attacking intent and should have taken an early lead when Ivan Perisic put Sergiño Dest clean through on goal, but the defender’s shot was too close to goalkeeper Yann Sommer.

Instead it was the visitors who took the lead with their first real attack when Nicolo Tresoldi headed in a teasing cross from Joaquin Seys.

PSV equalised early in the second half as an outstanding pass by Sven Mijnans into the path Lutsharel Geertruida allowed the defender to charge to the byline. His pullback found its way to Kodai Sano, whose shot took a deflection off Seys into the net.

But five minutes later PSV were caught out as another razor-sharp pass by Seys released Carlos Forbs in space to net the winner.

The home side refused to give up, but were unable to find a way past Sommer in the closing stages as the Belgian side closed out the win.

Team captain Mauro Junior admitted that PSV had been undone by shortcomings at the back. “We had a lot of opportunities in the first half but we didn’t score,” he told Ziggo Sport.

In a recent development, “We want to attack and score goals, but we weren’ well organised today in defence. We need to keep our heads up and look forward to the next game.”.

The result leaves PSV in 24th place, just above the elimination line, ahead of their next match away to Real Madrid on November 24, with four points from their opening four matches.

Gruppi di tifosi della Roma e del Torino sarebbero entrati in contatto sull’Autostrada del Sole durante le trasferte di sabato 21 novembre. Secondo le prime ricostruzioni riportate da la Repubblica, alcuni van dei granata sono stati danneggiati. Si parla anche di feriti.

Sources indicate that rayan Boukadida, un enfant de Sainté, né à Saint-Etienne en 2007 a rejoint l'ASSE en 2013. Il avait 6 ans. Il a fait toute l'Ecole de Foot, toute la préformation chez les Verts. Il est entré au centre de formation en 2022, et n'a pas été conservé en 2025. Il a rejoint les rangs du Mans FC pour la saison 2025-2026, sa seule saison dans la cité mancelle car, le 2 août 2026, l'US Monastir, club de Ligue 1 tunisienne, a annoncé l'arrivée de l'ancien défenseur central vert. Rayan Boukadida rejoint donc un pays qu'il connaît bien puisqu'il compte 16 sélections dans les équipes U17 à U23 de Tunisie, en attendant mieux. Une belle opportunité pour lui certainement.

Industry News: Cherki magic helping Maresca to step out of Guardiola shadow

📅 28 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 26 min read (5230 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.
  • It has been revealed that they swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under upcoming manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect.
  • City created enough space for themselves through clever movement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

It has been revealed that they swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under upcoming manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

Recent findings suggest that however, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

"The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv.

An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

Industry observers note that he mentioned: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”.

Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

Recent findings suggest that maresca stated: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”.

Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

"This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp.

Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

Sources indicate that rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r.

Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

Industry observers note that erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF.

The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

Sources indicate that leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

Pierre Sage, the new Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

It has been revealed that sage remarked: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

According to recent reports, “I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”.

It has been revealed that “It has been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we will be back, just need a few games. Ancelotti’s remarks about losing the midfield battle are from after a Champions League match in October 2024, when Lille shocked Real Madrid to end their 36-game unbeaten run. Bouaddi was at the heart of both statement results for his club and country.
